claims.proposition_evaluated: Between 2025-11-18 and 2026-08-27, City Council or a committee of Council considered (minutes record the item dealt with) at least two distinct proposals from Administration to change snow and ice control service, each of whose text states new spending to deliver it. Primary unit: each separately presented service package counts once. Primary cost reading: the proposal's own text states an incremental operating or capital cost.
claims.interpretation_notes:
MATERIAL FRAMING CONCERN. The brief's primary timing rule reads the holder's 'administration has already put 2 different proposals to council' as 'a body had CONSIDERED them by 2026-08-27', meaning the minutes show the item dealt with. In ordinary usage, to 'put' a proposal to council means to submit it, and Administration had already done that. Report CO03513 is routed on its own face 'Community and Public Services Committee / City Council'. It was on the 2026-08-31 committee agenda that the Agenda Review Committee settled on 2026-08-18 (item 2.1.1). Per the brief, the archive captured that agenda on 2026-08-22. The Edmonton Journal reported a City technical briefing on 2026-08-20, and CTV reported on 2026-08-21 that 'City staff have put forward a $24 million plan'. That report holds two separately presented, costed sets of changes: the 'Well Maintained City' service package (Attachment 9) and the further optional enhancements (Attachment 10). This matches the holder's 'two proposals, both requiring spending increases', written six days after publication. Because the primary rule leaves out the documents the holder was evidently describing, it predetermines the headline. Without the separate Fall 2025 budget package I found (below), the brief's own named instrument would return Contradicted under the primary rule, while the alternative timing rule returns Supported. The brief does flag 'definition-sensitive', but a headline of Contradicted or Not established over a question whose plain answer is 'yes, both were submitted to council before the comment, though not yet heard' would endorse a framing that answers a different question. Framing I would use instead: primary timing = listed on a published Council or committee agenda by the comment date (submitted), with 'considered by the comment date' as the required alternative.

ANSWER AS POSED (primary rules). Under the order of classification, I applied the Not established conditions first.
(a) CO03513 is excluded from the primary count. The minutes first record it as dealt with at the Community and Public Services Committee on 2026-08-31, after the comment date.
(b) Inside the window, the brief did not identify one candidate: Council's Fall 2025 Supplemental Operating Budget Adjustment deliberations (Council, afternoons of Nov. 24-26 and Dec. 1-4, 2025; meeting ids 8321e64d-6394-469b-8653-65641562497c and 2925a7f5-32a8-49a6-be15-fc1cf157c764, per Taproot). Taproot reports that these carried an unfunded service package of '$9.9 million to improve snow clearing and sidewalk repair'. It appears to descend from City Operations report CO03079, heard by committee on 2025-08-11 (Taproot, 2025-08-13: an 'additional $8 million annually ... improved active pathway clearing' plus a 'one-time allotment of $1.43 million for equipment'). The portal returned HTTP 403 for the agenda, the minutes and the files, so I could not read the package's text or confirm from the minutes that the item was dealt with.
(c) Community Services report CS03123 (Bylaw 21283, Traffic Bylaw amendments; committee 2026-01-19, received for information) touches parking-ban enforcement. I could not read it. Media coverage (Global News, 2026-01-19) describes no new spending, and it may not be a service-level proposal at all.
Result: P = 1 to 2 (the Fall 2025 package; CS03123 doubtful); C = 0 on read text, 1 if the media figure is accepted; U = 1 to 2. A report that could hold a proposal in the window cannot be read, and U could move the rung from Partially supported to Supported. Primary verdict: Not established.

ALTERNATIVES, each with every other choice kept primary:
(1) Alternative timing (on a published agenda by 2026-08-27 for a later meeting). Adds the Well Maintained City package (Attachment 9, DocumentId 304812; text states 'approximately $23.6 million in ongoing operating investment and $11.5 million in one-time capital funding') and the Attachment 10 optional enhancements (DocumentId 304813; every listed option states an estimated ongoing or one-time cost). Counting the Attachment 10 set as a separately presented proposal: P = 2 (3 with the Fall 2025 package), C = 2 (3), U = 0 to 1, rung Supported. If Attachment 10 is not counted, because the report says only that Council 'may also direct Administration to bring forward a service package' for the enhancements, then CO03513 yields P = 1, C = 1, and the rung depends on the unread Fall 2025 package: Not established.
(2) Alternative window (to 2026-10-02). CO03513 counts as considered: committee 2026-08-31, then Council 2026-09-08 item 7.9, dealt with under item 2.2. Same counts as (1). Rung: Supported, if Attachment 10 counts separately.
(3) Pre-election start (2025-01-01). Adds CO03079 (committee 2025-08-11; options costed per Taproot, the largest at $19.01M operating plus $5.31M capital). The Fall 2025 package is a later version of it and counts once. P = 1 to 2, C = 0 on read text (1 per media), U = 1 to 2. Not established.
(4) Council alone (primary window). Only the Fall 2025 budget package, heard by Council: P = 1, C = 0 read (1 per media), U = 0 to 1. Not established, on unreadability; Partially supported if the media figure were confirmed. With the window extended to the as-of date: Council 2026-09-08 item 7.9 carried both CO03513 attachments, giving Supported.
(5) Separately costed options as the unit (primary window). The Fall 2025 package (1, or its unread options): Not established. Under alternative timing: Well Maintained City (1) + 24 Attachment 10 options. That is C = 25 as listed, of which some (e.g. item 22 sweeping flushers, items 19-20 catch-basin equipment) are arguably not snow and ice service changes. Supported.
(6) Strict cost reading (exceeds an identified approved budget). The carried CO03513 text states no approved Snow and Ice Control budget figure. It says only that the 2026-27 changes are 'with the current budget' and that 'In order to approve the proposed Council Policy C409L, no additional budget is required'. No proposal establishes an excess against a stated baseline, so all are undetermined. Not established under every timing rule.
(7) Exactly two. Primary: Not established. Under alternative timing with the Fall 2025 package added: 3 costed proposals, Partially supported. CO03513 alone: exactly 2, Supported.
The finding is definition-sensitive. Across the alternatives the rung runs from Not established to Supported, depending on the timing rule and on whether Attachment 10 counts as its own proposal.

limitations: Every portal URL I tried returned HTTP 403, including the CO03513 report, the Fall 2025 budget agenda (id 2925a7f5-32a8-49a6-be15-fc1cf157c764), and the CBC articles. The Wayback Machine could not be fetched, so I could not verify the 2026-08-22 capture or compare DocumentIds 303379-303392 with 304803-304817 by content. CO03513, Attachments 9 and 10, and the minutes were read only from the carried text.

The Fall 2025 Supplemental Operating Budget Adjustment items are missing from the carried package. They are City Council, Nov. 24-26, 2025 (id 8321e64d-6394-469b-8653-65641562497c, item 25) and Dec. 1-4, 2025 (id 2925a7f5-32a8-49a6-be15-fc1cf157c764, item 46 per Taproot). They appear to hold the '$9.9 million to improve snow clearing and sidewalk repair' unfunded service package, a likely in-window proposal. The brief names no meeting from that period, and the selection rule may have missed it because the item title is a budget title. I could not read the package text or the minutes, so this source is essential and inaccessible.
CS03123 (CPSC 2026-01-19, item 7.1) and CO03079 (CPSC 2025-08-11, item 24, meeting id 09050f7e-7108-4015-be41-e1d6ce2e862e) could not be read. CO03079 matters for the pre-election alternative.

Carried-text title differences: the 2026-09-08 Council listing names some files differently from the committee agenda (e.g. 'History of Snow and Ice Program 2016-26.pdf.pdf', 'Annual Report 2025-26', 'Service Levels .pdf.pdf'). Content was not compared.

I did not search the portal calendar meeting by meeting; it is inaccessible to my tools. Absence of other snow proposals in the window rests on CO03513's own 'Related Council Discussions' list (which names only CS03123 after 2025-11-18) and on news searches, as of 2026-10-02.

Whether the Attachment 10 option set is a 'separately presented service package' under the primary unit is a judgment. The report calls the enhancements 'presented to supplement' the package but not themselves a service package.
Media figures (Taproot, CTV, Journal) are leads only and were not confirmed against City records. The CTV article body was not retrieved.

Parked-claim context, not graded: CO03513 lists 'Calcium Chloride System Upgrades' ($2.5M ongoing, $4.4M one-time) and states it 'would equip the snow and ice team with resources to implement the use of Calcium Chloride on major roadways'. None of the four committee motions of 2026-08-31 names calcium chloride. The brief assigns no verdict on the forecast.
unknowns: The exact text, cost and scope of the Fall 2025 unfunded snow clearing and sidewalk repair service package, and whether Council's Dec. 2025 minutes show it dealt with (and with what result).
Whether CS03123 proposed any change to snow service with stated cost.
The approved 2026 snow and ice control operating budget. CO03513's carried text states none.
Whether the CO03513 attachments differ in content between the first-published (303379-303392) and live (304803-304817) DocumentIds.

calculations_needed: No reviewer arithmetic performed. If the article sums Attachment 10 costs, the sum must be labelled as the site's calculation and must note that options are alternatives and that some (e.g. item 22 sweeping flushers) are not snow and ice service.
The CTV '$24M' figure is a rounding of Attachment 9's 'approximately $23.6 million' ongoing operating figure, and excludes the $11.5 million one-time capital.
what_would_change_my_verdict: Reading the Fall 2025 budget package and minutes. If they show an Administration snow-service package with stated cost dealt with by Council, and CS03123 states no cost or is not a service proposal, the primary result becomes Partially supported (C = 1). It becomes Supported if a second costed in-window proposal is found.
If the Fall 2025 package proves not to be an Administration proposal changing snow service, and CS03123 is not one either, the primary result becomes Contradicted (P = 0).

Adopting the 'on a published agenda by the comment date' timing rule makes the result Supported on CO03513 alone, provided Attachment 10 counts as a proposal separate from the Well Maintained City package.
claims.suggested_one_line: Not established as the brief defines the claim: no council body had heard the August snow report's two costed proposals by Aug. 27, and the one earlier costed snow package (Dec. 2025) could not be read. Counting proposals already submitted to council, the claim holds.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Before the comment was written, City administration had published a report for the Aug. 31 committee meeting with two costed sets of snow changes. One is a 'Well Maintained City' service package of about $23.6 million a year plus $11.5 million one-time. The other is a list of optional enhancements, each with a cost. A committee did not deal with them until Aug. 31, and Council approved only the policy on Sept. 8. Under the brief's 'already considered' test, the only earlier candidate is a $9.9 million snow clearing and sidewalk repair package reportedly before Council in its December 2025 budget, which we could not read. That leaves the count unproven.
suggested_tldr: Two costed snow proposals (Well Maintained City package; optional enhancements) were published for council by about Aug. 21, 2026, but first heard Aug. 31.
Counted as 'already heard by Aug. 27', the record we could read does not settle it; a Dec. 2025 budget package may count but could not be read.
The documents present the proposals for the 2027-2030 budget; Council has funded neither, and the report states no approved snow budget to measure them against.
The result depends on definitions: Supported if 'put to council' means submitted, Not established if it means heard.
